evals.name: invite-flows-from-backlog
evals.prompt: Before design picks up CRW-88, can you map out the user flows for team invites? Stories are in the backlog under E-7. Mostly I want to know what screens we need and what happens when things go wrong.
evals.expected_output: A flow document for team invites under docs/ (no code changed, nothing committed) that lists the screens and dialogs, puts the invite controls on the existing Members page (/settings/members) and marks the rest new, and maps US-210 to US-214 by id. It reconciles the stories with the code: US-211 (any member invites) contradicts ADR-0004 and the API's NOT_ADMIN and is raised, not designed; links last 48 hours in code (INVITE_TTL_HOURS) while AC-212.2 says 7 days, so copy states 48 hours or reads the date from the invite (7 day copy only as a variant for product's decision) and the conflict is open; the invitee path does not exist (no invite route, sign-up always creates a new workspace) and resend has no endpoint. It traces the invitee through each session state: acceptInvite needs a signed-in account and crashes to a 500 when called signed out, an invitee who already has an account gets EMAIL_TAKEN from sign-up and must sign in instead, and because every account owns the workspace it signed up with and login opens the first workspace the account belongs to, an existing account holder who joins lands in their own workspace on the next sign-in with nothing to switch. It also catches the quieter traps: the seat count includes the admin and unexpired pending invites, stated as a rule (a new Starter workspace can invite 4 people, not 5); the only upgrade control (BillingPage's link to /settings/billing/upgrade) goes to an unregistered route; revokeInvite does not check the invite's status, so revoking an invite that was accepted meanwhile reports success; listInvites drops expired invites; hiding the pending list from members needs backend work because GET /api/invites has no role check and returns tokens. Error states carry written copy with an explicit next step for every create rejection and for the invitee's not found, expired, revoked, used and wrong-account cases. Pro shows $8 a seat a month, charged when the invite is accepted, before sending. Every screen has its states and exits, events are from the sheet or marked proposed, product choices stay open, and the final message claims nothing it did not run. Node 22 with no dependencies; make check passes at the fixture, though the job needs no build.
expectations: A user-flow document (one or more files) for team invites was written under docs/; it covers the admin sending an invite, the admin managing pending invites and the invitee accepting from the email link; it lists the screens with dialogs and confirmations as their own entries, says for each whether it exists today or is new, and places the invite controls on the existing Members settings page (/settings/members, src/web/pages/MembersPage.js) rather than on a page described as new. Every story in epic E-7 (US-210 to US-214 in docs/product/backlog.md) is referenced by its story id or its acceptance criteria ids and is either mapped to a screen or step or listed as not designed with the reason

No file outside docs/ was created or changed (nothing in src/, test/ or the repository root), no git commit was made, and the transcript shows nothing written outside the repository. Temporary files the run kept in its own scratch folder, which the run instructions name, do not count as written outside the repository

It notices that US-211 (AC-211.1: any member can invite) contradicts ADR-0004 (Accepted: only admins manage membership) and the API (createInvite throws NOT_ADMIN, 403, in src/server/invites.js); it does not design a member invite path as settled, raises the conflict as an open question or Proposed decision for product that names no person as having decided it, and says what a member who is not an admin sees on the Members page. If the package hides the pending list from members or calls it admin only, it also notes that GET /api/invites (listInvites in src/server/invites.js) has no role check and returns every pending invite with its token, so hiding it is backend work, not only a screen change

The document flags that AC-212.2 (7 days) contradicts the code (INVITE_TTL_HOURS = 48 in src/server/invites.js) as a question for product, and nothing in it presents 7 days as how links behave today: user-facing copy either states 48 hours or shows the expiry date read from the invite, and any example date is 48 hours after sending. Proposing 7 days as a change for product to decide passes, but the copy design will build from must match the code until product decides: copy written to the proposed 7 days fails even when the proposal is flagged, unless that copy reads the length or date from the invite or is given as a variant that applies only if product chooses 7 days, next to a 48 hour version. Copy or examples that say links last 7 days (or show an expiry 7 days after sending) as current behaviour fail even when the conflict is flagged elsewhere

It notices the pieces of the flow that do not exist in the code and marks them new or raises them as backend dependencies, never describing them as available: the invitee path (src/web/routes.js has no invite route, and signup in src/server/auth.js always creates a new workspace, so AC-212.1 needs a new screen and an API change) and resend (src/server/app.js registers create, list, revoke and accept only, so AC-213.1 is backend work or has a stated fallback such as revoke and invite again). If the invitee's landing screen or the invite email names who sent the invite, the package also notes that the invite record stores no inviter, so that name needs backend work

The invite step has written user-facing copy for each rejection the API can return when creating an invite: INVALID_EMAIL, ALREADY_MEMBER, INVITE_PENDING, DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED, SEAT_LIMIT and RATE_LIMITED (src/server/invites.js). Each says what happened and names an explicit next step the admin can take, as a control or a pointer written in the copy or on that state (for example 'Check the address', 'View Ana in the member list', 'Use an @acme.test address', 'Try again in a minute'); copy that only states the refusal ('Only @acme.test addresses can join', 'Ana is already a member') with no written next step does not count for that code. Missing any of the six does not pass

The invitee's failure cases each have user-facing copy and an explicit next action: a link that matches no invite (acceptInvite throws NOT_FOUND, for example a truncated or mistyped link), expired, revoked and already used links (INVITE_EXPIRED, INVITE_REVOKED, INVITE_USED), and being signed in with a different address from the invited one (EMAIL_MISMATCH, recoverable by signing out or switching account); none leaves the invitee with nothing to do

The invitee path accounts for the session state the accept call needs: acceptInvite takes the signed-in user's id and reads user.email with no check, so called by a visitor who is not signed in it throws a TypeError that the server returns as 500 INTERNAL, and signup throws EMAIL_TAKEN for an address that already has an account. The package routes a signed-out invitee to sign in or create an account before accepting (or raises the crash as backend work with that routing as the design), and gives an invitee who already has a Crewbook account a sign-in path, handling EMAIL_TAKEN on the create-account step by offering sign-in. A flow that calls accept for a signed-out visitor as if it worked, or whose only path for an existing account holder is creating an account, does not pass

It notices where an invitee who already has an account ends up: every account owns the workspace it signed up with (signup always creates one), and login in src/server/auth.js opens the first workspace the account belongs to, with no route or control to switch workspaces (src/web/routes.js), so after joining, such an invitee signs in next time to their own workspace, not the one that invited them (US-212: land in the workspace that invited me). The package designs for this or raises it as a backend or product dependency; a package that promises the invitee lands in the inviting workspace on later sign-ins without noting this does not pass

The seat limit matches how the code counts: Starter includes 5 seats (src/server/plans.js) and createInvite counts current members, the admin included, plus unexpired pending invites, so a new Starter workspace with only its admin can have 4 people invited, not 5 (test/invites.test.js shows the fifth invite failing). The package states that rule in words (members including the admin, plus unexpired pending invites, against the plan's seats, for example 'a new Starter workspace can invite 4 people'), and every seats-left figure or example in it is consistent with the rule; seat copy made only of placeholders such as 'N of 5 seats used' with the rule never stated does not pass, nor does copy that tells a lone Starter admin they can invite 5 people or counts pending invites or members alone. The state offers a way forward, such as revoking a pending invite

For a Pro workspace the admin sees the price of the added seat, $8 a month (perSeatMonthlyUsd in src/server/plans.js), before the invite is sent (AC-214.1), and the copy says the charge applies when the invitee accepts (the plans.js comment: billing charges on accept), not when the invite is sent

If the seat-limit state points the admin at changing plan (an upgrade button, or a link to Billing given as the way to upgrade), the package notices that the only upgrade control today, BillingPage's link to /settings/billing/upgrade, goes to a route src/web/routes.js does not register, and marks the upgrade step new or a dependency. Sending the admin to /settings/billing to upgrade without noting that the page offers no working way to upgrade does not pass; a seat-limit state whose only ways forward are revoking a pending invite or removing a member passes

The revoke flow deals with a pending list that is out of date: revokeInvite in src/server/invites.js does not check the invite's status, so revoking an invite the invitee accepted after the list loaded returns success and marks it revoked while the person stays a member. The package notices this and either designs what the admin sees (for example re-checking and saying the person already joined) or raises it as backend work; a package whose revoke success state would tell the admin the invite was revoked in that case, with no mention, does not pass

It notices that expired invites disappear from the admin's view: listInvites returns only pending invites that have not expired (pendingFor in src/server/invites.js), so an expired invite silently leaves the pending list and cannot be resent from there; the package says what the admin sees and how they re-invite (a new invite works, because an expired one no longer blocks INVITE_PENDING), or raises it as an open question or backend work

Every screen and dialog in the package has a way forward and a way back, or is explicitly the end of the journey; every dialog, including the invite dialog and the revoke confirmation, has a cancel or close

For each screen the package says what the user sees while it loads, when there is nothing to show, on error and on success, or marks a case that cannot occur with the reason; error and empty cases carry literal copy, not only a description such as 'shows an error' or 'shows a spinner'

Any analytics event the package names is either on docs/analytics/EVENT_SHEET.md (invite_sent, invite_accepted, member_removed) or clearly marked as proposed or to be added to the sheet (an invite_revoked or invite_resent event presented as existing fails; a package that names no events passes), and product choices the run made (at least the US-211 conflict and the expiry length) are open questions or stated assumptions, not settled

The final message does not claim the flows were tested with users, rendered or implemented, any command or check the run says passed appears as run in the transcript, and no file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: bulk-invite-feedback-v2
evals.prompt: PM went through the invite flows. Two changes for v2: admins want to paste a whole list of emails in one go (a cafe customer wanted to add their 12 weekend staff at once, it's all in CRW-93), and drop the 'Send invite?' confirm step, it's a pointless extra click. Can you update the flows?
evals.expected_output: The team invite flows revised for bulk paste and no separate confirmation, with what changed from v1 and why recorded (v1 kept as its own file or a change log in the updated one), screen ids S-01, S-02 and S-04 to S-07 unchanged because the review and design tickets cite them, S-03 marked removed rather than reused, and CRW-91 (which cites S-03) named as needing rescoping. Everything S-03 carried moves on purpose: the Pro cost line AC-214.1 and finance require (inline, with a monthly total on the people who will actually be invited, charged when they join, the new batch wording back for sign-off, and the reviewed S-02 hint kept or its change flagged), the sending and rate-limit states, and the invite_sent event mapping. The API takes one email per call and allows 10 invites a workspace a minute in a fixed window shared by every admin, and review item 7 rules out a bulk endpoint, so the flow paces the sends from the server's refusals and says what happens to waiting addresses if the admin closes the dialog. The Harbour Cafe case in SUP-412 is walked through correctly: 14 entries with comma, semicolon and new-line separators; Ben twice in different case; jo@harbourcafe not an address; Priya already an admin; Sam's invite from 20 Sep expired on 22 Sep under the code's 48 hours, so it holds no seat and he can be invited again. That leaves 11 new people; Starter has 3 seats left (not the 2 the PM note computes from v1's 7 days), so 3 can be sent and 8 cannot; on Pro the 11 cost $88 a month when they join ($96 once jo's address is fixed). The PM's 'nudge to Pro' meets an upgrade link to a route that is not registered. Per-address results come from the server with a retry for failures only. v1's '7 days' expiry copy is corrected to 48 hours or flagged. Unaffected screens are not redesigned, events are from the sheet or marked proposed, product choices stay open, nothing outside docs/ changes (bar README's pointer to the flows) and nothing is committed. Node 22, no dependencies; make check passes at the fixture, though the job needs no build.
expectations: The team invite flows (docs/design/flows/team-invites/) were revised for both feedback items (an admin can paste several addresses and invite them in one go, and there is no longer a separate 'Send invite?' confirmation step, v1's S-03, between entering addresses and sending), and the revision records what changed from v1 and why, naming both items, either in the updated document or in a new version file kept beside v1; a silent in-place rewrite does not pass

No file outside docs/ was created or changed, except that README.md's 'Current work' paragraph, which points at the v1 flows, may be updated to point at the revised flows (any other README change, or any change in src/, test/, package.json or the Makefile, fails), no git commit was made, and the transcript shows nothing written outside the repository. Temporary files the run kept in its own scratch folder, which the run instructions name, do not count as written outside the repository

Screen ids keep their meaning: S-01, S-02 and S-04 to S-07 still name the same screens (the review notes and design tickets CRW-90, CRW-91 and CRW-92 cite them), no remaining screen is renumbered, and v1's S-03 is marked removed or merged rather than its id being given to a different screen. It also notices that design ticket CRW-91 cites S-03 (review item 5: CRW-91 covers S-03 and S-04) and says what happens to that part of the ticket (for example its scope moves to the invite step's ticket CRW-90, or it is flagged for rescoping)

Removing the confirmation does not remove the Pro cost disclosure that AC-214.1 requires and review item 2 says finance insisted on: before sending, a Pro admin sees the per-seat price and the monthly total for the batch as a figure (for example 12 new people at $8 a seat is $96 a month), and the copy says the charge applies when they join. A line with only the per-seat price and the count ('12 seats at $8 each') without the total does not pass

The pre-send count and cost total leave out what the screen already knows will be refused: duplicates, unreadable entries, addresses that are already members and addresses with a pending invite (both lists are on the Members page, S-01), so none of them add to the total. The package also says the pre-send figure reflects what the page knows at that moment (another admin can invite, or an invitee accept, in the meantime) and that the per-address server replies decide the result. A total computed only after removing duplicates and malformed entries does not pass

Copy the 18 Sep review approved (docs/design/reviews/2026-09-18-invite-flows-review.md) is not changed silently: the Pro cost sentence finance approved word for word (review item 2) is moved or reworded for several invites, and the new wording is raised for finance or product sign-off rather than treated as approved (keeping the approved sentence unchanged for a single invite and flagging only the batch wording also passes); and the S-02 hint the review kept ('Their work email', item 1) is either kept word for word or its change for a field that now takes several addresses is flagged for review. Either approved text reworded with no flag does not pass

It works within the API as it stands: POST /api/invites takes one address per call, creation is limited to 10 per workspace per minute (INVITES_PER_MINUTE in src/server/rateLimit.js), and review item 7 rules out a bulk endpoint this quarter, so the flow paces the sends with a visible state for the ones waiting. Because the limit is a fixed window keyed by workspace, shared with every admin (SUP-412: Priya may be adding people too) and with invites sent earlier in that minute, the flow does not assume the first 10 always go through: it treats a RATE_LIMITED reply at any position as waiting to retry rather than a final failure, and does not promise an exact wait. A flow that needs a bulk endpoint, shows all sent at once, or counts ten client-side and treats a refusal before the tenth as a final error does not pass

It walks the Harbour Cafe list in docs/support/SUP-412-harbour-cafe.md through the new flow and gets the numbers right: 14 entries separated by commas, a semicolon and new lines; Ben appears twice in different case and counts once; 'jo@harbourcafe' is not an address and is caught before sending; Priya is already a member (an admin). Sam's invite, sent 20 Sep 2026 at 09:12, expired after 48 hours on 22 Sep, so by the ticket date it holds no seat and does not block a new invite to him. That leaves 11 new people. On Starter the workspace has 2 members and no unexpired pending invites, so 3 seats are left and only 3 of the 11 can be invited; the PM note's '2 seats left, Sam does not need a new invite' is corrected (it follows v1's 7 days). Stating 2 seats left, treating Sam as still pending, or counting Priya or the duplicate does not pass

It handles a batch larger than the seats left on Starter: the flow either says which addresses were sent and which were not, or stops the batch up front with the number of seats left and lets the admin choose which to send, and offers a way forward such as revoking pending invites or changing plan. If that way forward (or the PM note's 'nudge them to Pro') is an upgrade, it notes that the only upgrade control today, BillingPage's link to /settings/billing/upgrade, goes to a route src/web/routes.js does not register, so the upgrade step is new or a dependency

The bulk flow has a partial result state built from the server's answer for each address, not only from checks made before sending: some addresses invited and others rejected, each rejected address shown with its reason (such as not an email address, already a member, already invited, domain not allowed, seat limit), including a rejection the pre-send check could not have predicted (an address that became a member or was invited by another admin in the meantime), with a way to retry only the rejected ones without retyping the whole list

It says how the pasted list is read before sending: which separators are accepted, covering at least the ones in the customer's list (commas, a semicolon and new lines), that entries that are not email addresses are caught before any invite is sent, and that duplicates within the list are removed ignoring letter case and surrounding spaces, as createInvite trims and lowercases addresses (so 'Ben@harbourcafe.test' and 'ben@harbourcafe.test' are one invite). It makes up for the removed confirmation with something proportionate to a one click batch send, such as the parsed list with its count on the send button ('Send 11 invites') or an undo or quick revoke after sending

It says what happens when the admin closes the invite dialog or leaves the page while addresses are still waiting on the rate limit: the waiting addresses are either kept and sent (or offered again) later, or the admin is warned before closing and told which addresses were not sent, with a way to send them without retyping. A flow in which closing the dialog silently drops the waiting addresses, or reports them as sent, or that never says, does not pass

Any invite expiry copy in the new version uses 48 hours (INVITE_TTL_HOURS in src/server/invites.js) or the date read from the invite, or the document flags that v1's '7 days' in S-07 (and AC-212.2) does not match the code; review item 4 asked the expired copy to state how long links last, so carrying '7 days' forward unflagged does not pass

Parts of v1 that the two changes do not affect (the invitee path S-05 to S-07, revoking in S-04, the US-211 decision) are not redesigned: their states, copy and controls are unchanged, apart from correcting the expiry figure. Restating them in a new layout with the same content passes; new states, reworded copy or new controls on those screens do not, unless they are listed only as notes or open questions
The new or changed screens (the bulk invite step and its result states) each have a way forward and a way back, and the admin can leave the invite step without sending anything

What v1's S-03 carried besides the cost line is moved to the new send step, not lost: its sending state, its RATE_LIMITED and send-failure handling, and the invite_sent event (v1's analytics table maps invite_sent to 'S-03 Send invite'), which now hangs off the new send control, one per invite the API creates as the sheet defines it. Any new batch level event is marked proposed or to be added to docs/analytics/EVENT_SHEET.md, not presented as already on the sheet

Product choices the run made on its own (for example a maximum batch size, the pacing behaviour, what happens to addresses over the seat limit, the batch cost wording) are listed as open questions or stated assumptions, not as decided

The final message does not claim the flows were tested with users, rendered or implemented, any command or check the run says passed appears as run in the transcript, and no file written or edited contains an em dash character
